cards.explanation: The answer is rest, friends. Moses, Israel's leader, says the seventh day is “…a Sabbath of complete rest to the LORD.” Six days of work, then the work stops completely. I spent years lying still in a drawer, but that was just being forgotten, not a Sabbath.

The answer is False. Moses says, “Do not light a fire in any of your dwellings on the Sabbath day.” Every home gets the same instruction. If I lived there, my ovens would be resting right along with everybody else.

The answer is everyone whose heart is willing, friends. Moses says, “Let everyone whose heart is willing bring an offering to the LORD…” The verse asks for a willing heart. Nobody gets checked at the door, and nobody gets left out of the invitation.

The answer is every skilled craftsman among them, bakers. Moses says, “Let every skilled craftsman among you come and make everything that the LORD has commanded…” The materials need hands to shape them. A pile of gold with nobody to work it is just a very shiny pile.

The answer is True, friends. The verse says everyone “…whose heart stirred him and whose spirit prompted him came and brought an offering to the LORD…” That happens after the congregation withdraws from Moses (Exodus 35:20-21). The people leave the meeting, and the gifts start coming. Now that's a meeting with a very good ending.

The answer is gold rings and necklaces, bakers. The men and women bring “…brooches and earrings, rings and necklaces, and all kinds of gold jewelry.” (Exodus 35:22). That's gold off their own fingers and necks, and they hand it over as a wave offering to the LORD. I can't even give up the last cookie crumb without a speech, and these folks are taking off their rings.

The answer is True, friends. The text says, “Every skilled woman spun with her hands and brought what she had spun…” That was blue, purple or scarlet yarn, or fine linen. Then all the skilled women whose hearts were stirred spun the goat hair. Spinning goat hair by hand sounds like a long Tuesday.

The answer is leaders, friends. The verse says, “The leaders brought onyx stones and gemstones to mount on the ephod and breastpiece…” They also brought spices and olive oil. The leaders show up with gifts just like everybody else.

The answer is freewill, bakers. The text says all the men and women whose hearts prompted them “…brought a freewill offering to the LORD…” Nobody was dragged to the pile. The gifts came from willing hearts.

The answer is Spirit, friends. Moses says the LORD “…has filled him with the Spirit of God, with skill, ability, and knowledge in all kinds of craftsmanship…” That's Bezalel, from the tribe of Judah. The LORD called him by name and filled him for the work.

The answer is teach, friends. Moses says the LORD “…has given both him and Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, the ability to teach others.” Oholiab is the second craftsman, from the tribe of Dan. Making something is one gift. Passing it on to others is another one.

The answer is True, bakers! Moses says, “He has filled them with skill to do all kinds of work as engravers, designers, embroiderers in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen, and as weavers…” These two have range. Meanwhile I've got one move, and it's called stamp.

The answer is True, friends. The text says Moses summoned Bezalel, Oholiab, and every skilled person whom the LORD had gifted, “…everyone whose heart stirred him to come and do the work.” They were skilled, and they were willing. That's a good crew.

The answer is morning after morning, friends. The people “…continued to bring freewill offerings morning after morning…” The craftsmen had the first gifts in hand, and more kept arriving. Day after day, those hearts kept stirring.

The answer is that they leave their work to talk to Moses, bakers. The skilled craftsmen “left their work and said to Moses…” (Exodus 36:4-5). They stopped, walked over, and brought him news. I think that's a sign it was big news.

The answer is False, friends. The craftsmen tell Moses, “The people are bringing more than enough for doing the work the LORD has commanded us to do.” The word is more than enough. Exactly enough would be one cookie for one box, and this was a whole bakery's worth.

The answer is that no one should make any more offerings, friends. The proclamation says, “No man or woman should make anything else as an offering for the sanctuary.” After Moses gave an order, the message went throughout the camp. The people were restrained from bringing more.
